name: Australia
description: Australia offers expats a high quality of life, strong job opportunities, and a relaxed, outdoor-oriented lifestyle. Its diverse cities provide excellent amenities, though the cost of living, particularly housing, can be high. The country continues to attract skilled migrants and international students.
longdescription: Australia is a highly sought-after destination for expatriates, known for its welcoming culture and strong economy. The society is largely egalitarian and values honesty, humility, and fairness. Expats often find Australians to be friendly and informal, embracing a 'no worries' attitude and a passionate sporting culture. Major cities like Sydney, Melbourne, and Perth consistently rank high for livability, offering vibrant cultural scenes, diverse food, and ample opportunities for outdoor activities, from beaches to national parks. The economy is robust and open, having shown resilience post-COVID-19, with strong growth and a demand for skilled workers. While the cost of living, especially accommodation in major cities, is considerable, it is often offset by high average salaries and a world-class healthcare system. English is the national language, but over 300 languages are spoken in Australian homes, reflecting its multicultural population. Safety is generally high, with low crime rates and well-monitored public transport systems, though awareness of local conditions and general safety practices is always advised.

visas.name: Student visa (subclass 500)
visas.description: The Student visa (subclass 500) allows international students to study full-time at a registered Australian education provider. This visa covers various types of study, from English language courses and vocational training to undergraduate and postgraduate university programs, and permits a stay for the duration of the course.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an international student who intends to pursue full-time study at an Australian education or training provider registered with CRICOS.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Student visa (subclass 500) itself is a temporary visa, but it can be the initial step towards permanent residency. After completing studies, eligible graduates may apply for a Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485) to gain work experience in Australia. This experience and Australian qualifications can then contribute to eligibility for skilled migration visas (e.g., Subclass 189, 190, or 491) or employer-sponsored permanent visa pathways, subject to meeting specific criteria like points tests and Skilled Occupation Lists.
benefits: Ability to study a full-time course at a registered Australian education provider.
Permission to work up to 48 hours per fortnight during study sessions, with unlimited hours during scheduled course breaks.
Option to include eligible family members (spouse/partner and dependent children under 18) in the visa application.
Freedom to travel in and out of Australia while the visa is valid.
Potential pathway to permanent residency in Australia after completing studies and meeting further eligibility criteria.
required_documents: Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) from a CRICOS-registered Australian education provider.
Valid passport copy and national identity card.
Evidence of financial capacity to cover tuition fees, living costs, and travel.
Proof of English language proficiency (unless exempt).
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the entire duration of the stay.
Genuine Student (GS) statement/responses.
Academic transcripts.
Statement of Purpose (SOP).
Health examination results (if requested).
Biometrics (if required).
Birth certificates for dependent children and marriage certificate for spouse/partner (if applicable).
Consent letter(s) from non-accompanying parent(s) for minors (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Receive a Letter of Offer from an Australian education provider.
Obtain a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) after accepting the offer and paying the deposit.
Gather all required documents, including proof of financial capacity, English language proficiency, OSHC, and prepare your Genuine Student (GS) responses.
Apply online through an ImmiAccount on the official Department of Home Affairs website.
Complete any required health examinations and biometrics.
Track your visa application status and respond to any requests for additional information.

visas.name: Student Guardian visa (subclass 590)
visas.description: The Student Guardian visa (subclass 590) allows a parent, legal custodian, or eligible relative to come to Australia to provide care and support for an international student. This visa is temporary and is primarily for guardians of students under 18 years of age, though exceptions can be made for older students with exceptional circumstances.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a parent, legal custodian, or a relative aged 21 or older, who intends to provide accommodation, welfare, and support to an international student (typically under 18) studying in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is a temporary visa and does not provide a direct pathway to Australian permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the criteria for the visa, typically by applying for a further Student Guardian visa if the student's visa is extended.
benefits: Ability to reside in Australia for the duration of the student's course, tied to their visa validity.
Provide care and support for one or more student visa holders who are family members.
Opportunity to study an English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students (ELICOS) for less than 20 hours per week, or any other study or training for no more than 3 months.
Travel to and from Australia multiple times while the visa is valid.
required_documents: Passport and identity documents.
Proof of relationship to the student (e.g., birth certificates, legal custody documents).
Evidence of sufficient financial capacity to support yourself, the student, and any accompanying children.
Proof of adequate health insurance (Overseas Visitor Health Cover - OVHC) for the duration of stay.
Genuine Temporary Entrant (GTE) statement outlining the purpose and temporary nature of the stay.
Welfare and accommodation arrangements for the student.
Character documents (police clearances).
Form 157N - Student guardianship arrangements.
Consent form (Form 1229) or statutory declaration if one parent is not coming to Australia with the child.
application_process_steps: Check eligibility criteria for the visa.
Gather all required documents, including identity, relationship, financial, health insurance, and character documents.
Complete health examinations.
Lodge the application online through an ImmiAccount, ideally at least six weeks before the student's course starts.
Pay the visa application fee.
Respond to any requests for further information from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Training visa (subclass 407)
visas.description: The Training visa (subclass 407) allows individuals to come to Australia temporarily to participate in workplace-based occupational training or professional development. This visa is designed to enhance skills for a current occupation, area of tertiary study, field of expertise, or to fulfill professional development training programs.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals who need to undertake structured workplace-based training to improve their skills, obtain professional registration, or engage in professional development in an eligible occupation.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Training visa (subclass 407) does not offer a direct pathway to permanent residency. However, the Australian work experience, enhanced skills, and employer connections gained through this visa can significantly improve eligibility for other permanent residency visas, such as the Skills in Demand (Subclass 482) visa, Employer Nomination Scheme (Subclass 186) visa, Skilled Independent (Subclass 189) visa, or Skilled Nominated (Subclass 190) visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You may be eligible for another visa at the end of your 407.
benefits: Participate in structured workplace-based occupational training or professional development in Australia.
Stay in Australia for up to 2 years, depending on the training program.
Travel to and from Australia multiple times while the visa is valid.
Include eligible family members in the visa application.
Gain Australian work experience which can strengthen future PR prospects.
required_documents: Identity documents (proof of identity)
Sponsor approval letter (if applicable)
Sponsor's nomination approval letter (if sponsor is not a Commonwealth Government agency)
Written statement from the sponsor confirming meeting sponsorship obligations, including providing agreed training.
Evidence of financial capacity to support self and family in Australia.
Health insurance documentation (adequate Overseas Visitor Health Cover (OVHC)).
Evidence of English language proficiency (functional English).
Workplace-based activity documents (for occupational training streams).
Professional Development documents (for professional development stream).
Character documents (police clearances).
Partner documents (if including a partner).
Dependants under 18 documents (if including minor dependants).
Dependants over 18 documents (if including adult dependants).
A structured training plan relevant to the nominated occupation.
Evidence of at least 12 months full-time work or study experience in the nominated occupation within the past 24 months (for skills development stream).
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet the eligibility criteria, including being at least 18 years old (unless exempt), meeting health and character requirements, having functional English, and having adequate health insurance.

Have an approved sponsor (a business, organisation, or government agency) and an approved nomination (if the sponsor is not a Commonwealth Government agency) for a structured training program. This must be approved before the visa application is lodged.
Gather all required documents, including identity, financial support, health insurance, English language, character, and training-specific documents.
Lodge your visa application online, either from inside or outside Australia.
Pay the visa application fee.
Await processing and respond promptly to any requests for additional information from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485)
visas.description: The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) is a temporary visa designed for international students who have recently graduated from an Australian institution with an eligible qualification. It allows them to live, work, and study in Australia temporarily after completing their studies, providing an opportunity to gain valuable Australian work experience and potentially transition to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: International students who have recently completed a CRICOS-registered course at an Australian educational institution and hold an eligible visa, typically a Student visa (subclass 500), within the last six months.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Temporary Graduate visa acts as a bridge, allowing graduates to gain Australian work experience, improve English language skills, and meet criteria for various permanent residency pathways such as Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189), Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190), Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491 leading to 191 PR), or employer-sponsored visas (e.g., subclass 186, 494).
benefits: Stay in Australia temporarily after studies for a period ranging from 18 months to 5 years, depending on the stream and qualification.
Full work rights with no hourly restrictions, allowing graduates to gain Australian work experience.
Ability to travel in and out of Australia while the visa is valid.
Opportunity to include eligible family members (partner, child, or partner's child) in the application.
Can be a pathway to permanent residency through skilled migration or employer-sponsored visas.
required_documents: Valid passport
Evidence of adequate health insurance (Overseas Visitor Health Cover - OVHC)
Evidence of application for an Australian Federal Police check
Evidence of English language proficiency
Certified copy of academic transcripts and completion letter for eligible Australian qualification
Evidence of having held a Student visa in the last 6 months (or other eligible visa at time of application)
Identity documents
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility under the correct visa stream and meet age, study, and English language requirements.
Gather all required documentation, including passport, academic records, health insurance, and police check application evidence.
Complete English language test (if required) and obtain a skills assessment if applying for the Post-Vocational Education Work Stream.
Lodge the visa application online through ImmiAccount within six months of course completion.
Undertake any required health examinations and character checks.
Await the decision on the visa application.

visas.name: Adoption visa (subclass 102)
visas.description: The Adoption visa (subclass 102) allows children adopted outside Australia, or in the process of being adopted, to live permanently in Australia with their adoptive parent(s). This permanent visa facilitates family reunification and grants the adopted child access to Australian healthcare, education, and a pathway to citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is ideal for children under 18 years old who have been adopted or are in the process of being adopted by an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, with the child residing outside Australia at the time of application and visa grant.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Adoption visa (subclass 102) is a permanent visa, granting indefinite stay in Australia. Holders may apply for Australian citizenship once they meet the residency requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: After 5 years, the child will need to apply for a Resident Return Visa (RRV) to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Australian resident tax rules apply, as no special tax treatment is mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia.
Ability to work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Access to Australia's public healthcare scheme (Medicare).
Pathway to Australian citizenship, if eligible.
Travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date the visa is granted.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., passport, birth certificate, photos).
Legal adoption papers or proof of an ongoing adoption process.
Proof of sponsor's Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or eligible New Zealand citizenship.
Medical examination results (valid for 12 months).
Police clearance certificates (if applicable, for those over 16 years old and/or resided in a country for 12+ months).
Written consent from the child's biological parents (if required).
Evidence of Assurance of Support (AoS).
application_process_steps: Ensure the child and adoptive parents meet all eligibility criteria for the visa and adoption.
Gather all necessary documents, including identity, adoption, sponsorship, health, and character documents.
Complete the visa application form accurately while the child is outside Australia.
Lodge the visa application (online via ImmiAccount from July 23, 2025, or by paper previously) with all required documents.
Pay the visa application fee.
Await processing and respond to any requests for additional information from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Aged Dependent Relative visa (subclass 114)
visas.description: The Aged Dependent Relative visa (subclass 114) is a permanent visa designed for a single older person who lives outside Australia and is financially dependent on a close relative living in Australia. It allows them to move to Australia permanently and reunite with their sponsoring family member.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a single, older individual who is financially dependent on an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, and must be outside Australia when applying and when the visa is granted.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia. After meeting residency requirements, holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: This is a permanent visa; however, the travel facility typically has a 5-year validity and would need renewal to re-enter Australia after that period.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely (permanent residency).
Work and study in Australia.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible relatives to come to Australia.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., passport, birth certificate).
Evidence of your relationship to your sponsor.
Evidence your sponsor is an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen.
Proof of financial dependency on your sponsor for at least three years.
Completed Form 40 (Sponsorship for migration to Australia).
Completed Form 47OF (Application for migration to Australia by other family members).
Health examination results.
Police certificates from each country lived in for 12 months or more during the past 10 years.
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility with a sponsoring relative in Australia.
Gather all required documents.
Complete the visa application form (Form 47OF) and sponsor form (Form 40).
Lodge the visa application (typically by mail or courier as it's a paper application for offshore subclass 114).
Pay the visa application fee in two installments.
Await visa decision and respond to any additional requests for information.

visas.name: Aged Dependent Relative visa (subclass 838)
visas.description: The Aged Dependent Relative visa (subclass 838) is a permanent visa for a single older person who relies on a relative living in Australia for financial support. It allows them to stay in Australia indefinitely with their sponsoring relative.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an elderly individual who is single, meets the Australian Age Pension age requirement, and has been wholly or substantially financially dependent on an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen for their basic needs for at least three years.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency directly upon approval. After meeting specific residency requirements, visa holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: This is a permanent visa, allowing indefinite stay. However, a Resident Return visa (RRV) is required to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident after the initial 5-year travel facility expires.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely as a permanent resident.
Work and study in Australia.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible relatives to come to Australia.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Valid passport and birth certificate (identity documents).
Evidence of financial dependency on the sponsoring relative for at least three years (e.g., bank transfers, shared living expenses).
Sponsorship documents from an eligible Australian relative, including the completed Sponsorship Form.
Health examination results.
Police clearance certificates from countries lived in for 12 months or longer in the last 10 years.
Assurance of Support (AoS) from the sponsor, if required.
application_process_steps: Assess eligibility, ensuring all age, relationship, dependency, health, and character requirements are met.
Gather all necessary documents, including identity, financial dependency, sponsorship, health, and character documents.
The sponsoring relative completes the sponsorship form and provides an Assurance of Support, if required.
Complete and lodge the visa application form while in Australia (but not in immigration clearance).
Pay the visa application fee, which may be in two instalments.
Await processing and decision. The Department of Home Affairs will notify if additional information is needed, and may request interviews, health checks, or biometrics.

visas.name: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804)
visas.description: The Aged Parent visa (subclass 804) is a permanent visa that allows aged parents of settled Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens to live in Australia indefinitely. This visa is a non-contributory option, meaning it has a lower application fee but significantly longer processing times compared to contributory parent visas.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an elderly parent who is already in Australia (but not in immigration clearance) and has an eligible child who is a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, and meets the age and balance of family test requirements.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is a permanent visa, granting indefinite stay in Australia. After holding permanent residency for a qualifying period and meeting residency requirements, visa holders may become eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: After the initial 5-year travel facility, to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident, you will need to apply for and be granted a Resident Return Visa (RRV).
visas.tax_implications: You will not be entitled to automatically receive most social security payments or the age pension for a waiting period (two years for most social security payments, ten years for age and disability pension payments).
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely as a permanent resident
Work and study in Australia
Enroll in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare
Sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia
If eligible, attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program
required_documents: Completed visa and sponsorship forms
Proof of meeting eligibility criteria
Health examination results
Police certificates/character checks from countries lived in
Documents for dependents (if applicable)
Balance-of-Family documents
Assurance of Support details
Australian Values Statement (to sign)
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet eligibility criteria, including being in Australia (not in immigration clearance) at the time of application
Have an eligible sponsor who is a settled Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen
Gather and prepare all required documentation, including proof of meeting the Balance of Family Test
Lodge the visa and sponsorship application online using ImmiAccount and pay the first installment of the visa application fee
Your application will be assessed for eligibility and, if successful, placed in a queue for processing
Once requested, the sponsor must provide an Assurance of Support and pay a refundable security bond
Pay the second installment of the visa application fee when requested, before the visa can be granted

visas.name: Carer visa (subclass 116)
visas.description: The Carer visa (subclass 116) is a permanent visa that allows individuals outside Australia to move to Australia to provide ongoing substantial care and support for a relative with a long-term medical condition. This relative must have no reasonable access to other care options in Australia.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is someone outside Australia willing and able to provide long-term care to an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen who has a long-term medical condition and cannot receive adequate care through other means in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia, allowing the holder to live indefinitely in the country and apply for Australian citizenship if eligible.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely.
Work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare (after visa grant).
Sponsor relatives to come to Australia (if eligible).
Apply for Australian citizenship (if eligible).
required_documents: Completed Form 47OF Application for migration to Australia by other family members.
Identity documents (e.g., birth certificate, passport).
Proof of relationship with the sponsor and care recipient.
Sponsor's completed sponsorship form and documents.
Bupa medical certificate for the person requiring care, confirming their long-term medical condition and need for care.
Evidence the applicant is willing and able to provide ongoing care.
Character documents (police certificates, if requested).
Two recent passport-size photographs of the applicant and any other person included in the application.
Evidence of current marital status.
Original Curriculum Vitae for each person aged 18 years or over included in the application.
Proof of financial dependency for dependants over 18 (e.g., bank statements, money transfers).
application_process_steps: Check eligibility criteria for both the applicant and the sponsor.
Gather all necessary documents, including medical assessments, identity, relationship, and character documents.
Have the Australian relative complete the sponsorship form.
Complete the visa application form (Form 47OF) and attach all required documents.
Lodge the visa application (by mail or courier, typically to the Perth Visa and Citizenship Office for applicants from specific regions) and pay the visa application fee.
Await the visa decision from the Department of Home Affairs, noting that the visa is subject to an annual cap and a queueing system.

visas.name: Carer visa (subclass 836)
visas.description: The Carer visa (subclass 836) is a permanent visa for individuals already in Australia who wish to provide ongoing, substantial care to an Australian relative with a long-term medical condition. This visa is granted when the relative has no reasonable access to other care options within Australia.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an individual currently in Australia who is willing and able to provide long-term care to an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen relative who has a significant medical condition and cannot receive care from other sources.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Carer visa (subclass 836) is a permanent visa, directly granting permanent residency in Australia. After meeting certain residency requirements (typically 4 years of lawful residence, including 12 months as a permanent resident), visa holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: As a permanent visa, it does not require renewal. However, the travel facility granted with the visa is for 5 years, after which a Resident Return Visa (RRV) may be required to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Australian resident tax rules apply. No special tax treatments are mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia.
Full work rights in Australia.
Ability to study in Australia.
Access to Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Opportunity to sponsor other eligible relatives to come to Australia.
Pathway to Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
required_documents: Proof of identity (e.g., passport, birth certificate)
Police certificates from any country lived in for 12 months or more over the past 10 years (since turning 16)
Bupa medical certificate confirming the Australian relative's need for care due to a medical condition
Evidence that the Australian relative has no reasonable access to care in Australia from other sources
Proof of relationship to the Australian relative needing care
Evidence of willingness and ability to provide ongoing substantial care
Completed application form (Form 470F or equivalent, can be imported to ImmiAccount from July 2025)
Sponsorship by an eligible Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen relative (or their partner)
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility criteria are met for both the applicant and the Australian relative requiring care, including being in Australia at the time of application and decision.
Obtain sponsorship from an eligible Australian relative, who must be an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen.

Gather all necessary documents, including identity proofs, police certificates, medical certificates for the relative (from Bupa Medical Visa Services), and evidence of the care needs and lack of alternative care options.
Complete the application form (Form 470F) and submit it along with all supporting documents and pay the first instalment of the visa application fee.
Respond to any requests for further information from the Department of Home Affairs, including potentially paying a second instalment of the visa application fee.
Await a decision on the application while remaining in Australia.

visas.name: Child visa (subclass 101)
visas.description: The Child visa (subclass 101) is a permanent visa that allows a dependent child, who is outside Australia, to move to Australia and live permanently with their eligible parent(s). This visa supports family reunification and provides the child with the rights and benefits of an Australian permanent resident.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is ideal for dependent biological, adopted, or stepchildren of an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, who wish to live permanently in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency from the outset. After a qualifying period of residence and meeting other eligibility criteria, the visa holder may apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa grants permanent residency, so it does not expire. However, the initial travel facility is valid for 5 years. To re-enter Australia as a permanent resident after this period, the holder must apply for a Resident Return (RRV) visa or obtain Australian citizenship.
visas.tax_implications: Once granted permanent residency, the child will generally be considered an Australian resident for tax purposes, subject to Australia's standard tax rules on worldwide income. No special tax treatments are explicitly noted for this visa subclass.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely (permanent residency).
Work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor relatives to come to Australia (subject to eligibility).
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Child's birth certificate and identity documents (e.g., passport bio page).
Proof of parent-child relationship (e.g., birth certificate, adoption certificate, family book).
Parental consent documents, if the child is under 18 and not all legally responsible parents are migrating.
Evidence of financial dependency for children aged 18 to under 25 (e.g., bank statements, money transfers, rent receipts).
Evidence of full-time study for children aged 18 to under 25 (e.g., confirmation of enrolment, academic records).
Health examination reports.
Police clearance certificates for applicants and sponsors aged 16 or over, from each country lived in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years.
Sponsor's identity and proof of Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or eligible New Zealand citizenship.
Completed application forms (Form 47CH and Form 40CH).
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility criteria for both the child and the sponsoring parent.
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are complete and certified where necessary.
Complete and sign the mandatory application forms (Form 47CH for the child and Form 40CH for sponsorship).
Lodge the paper-based visa application (from 23 July 2025, applications can be imported into ImmiAccount after lodgement). The child must be outside Australia when the application is made.
Pay the application fee.
Undergo health examinations and provide character documents (e.g., police clearances) as requested by the Department of Home Affairs.
Await the visa decision while the child remains outside Australia.

visas.name: Child visa (subclass 802)
visas.description: The Child visa (subclass 802) is a permanent visa that allows an eligible dependent child to live indefinitely in Australia with their Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen parent(s). This visa is specifically for children who are already in Australia when the application is made and when the decision is granted.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a dependent child of an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, who is currently located in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Child visa (subclass 802) is a permanent visa, granting the child permanent residency in Australia from the outset. After meeting certain residency and other requirements, the child may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
benefits: Stay in Australia permanently.
Work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor relatives to come to Australia (if eligible).
Apply for Australian citizenship (if eligible).
required_documents: Child's valid passport and birth certificate.
Proof of relationship to the sponsoring parent (e.g., birth or adoption records).
Evidence of financial dependence if the child is over 18.
Health examination results and character assessment documents (e.g., Form 80 for children over 16, police certificates from countries lived in for 12+ months in the past 10 years).
Sponsor's proof of Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or eligible New Zealand citizenship.
Consent from anyone who can legally decide where the child lives (if under 18), or evidence that laws allow the child to leave their home country.
Application forms (e.g., Form 47CH for child, Form 40CH for sponsor).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, including identity, relationship, dependency, health, and character evidence.
The application is lodged online through the Department of Home Affairs ImmiAccount by the sponsoring parent.
Pay the application fee.
The application undergoes assessment, including health and character checks.
Receive a decision from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864)
visas.description: The Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864) is a permanent visa for older parents of settled Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens. It allows parents to live indefinitely in Australia, provided they meet specific age and family criteria and make a significant financial contribution.
visas.target_applicant: Aged parents of Australian citizens, permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens who are settled in Australia and can meet the balance of family test, and are able to pay a substantial visa application charge.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864) is a permanent residency visa allowing indefinite stay in Australia. Holders can apply for Australian citizenship once they meet the general residency requirements, typically after living in Australia as a permanent resident for a specified period (e.g., 5 years).
visas.renewal_conditions: After five years from the date the visa is granted, holders will need a Resident Return Visa (subclass 155 or 157) or another visa to re-enter Australia if they travel overseas.
visas.tax_implications: The 'contributory' aspect of this visa involves a significant financial payment to the Australian Government, which is intended to help offset the future costs that parents might incur on Australia's health and welfare systems, effectively compensating for taxes not paid as lifelong residents. Once granted permanent residency, standard Australian resident tax rules would apply.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely.
Work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme (Medicare).
Sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
Travel to and from Australia for five years from visa grant (renewable via Resident Return Visa).
required_documents: Proof of identity (for applicant, partner, and any dependents)
Evidence of relationship with sponsoring child (e.g., birth certificates, adoption papers)
Sponsor's identity and eligibility documents (must be 18+, settled Australian citizen/PR/eligible NZ citizen)
Evidence of meeting the 'balance of family' test
Health examination results
Police certificates (character requirements)
Assurance of Support documents (from sponsor)
Signed Australian Values Statement
Evidence of health insurance coverage (during processing, if not yet on Medicare)
application_process_steps: Check eligibility requirements, including age, sponsor, and balance of family test.
Gather all required documents, including identity, relationship, health, and character evidence.
Lodge the visa application online using ImmiAccount.
Pay the first instalment of the visa application charge.
Provide any additional information or documents requested by the Department of Home Affairs.
Pay the second, larger instalment of the visa application charge when requested, prior to visa grant.

visas.name: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143)
visas.description: The Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143) is a permanent visa that allows parents of settled Australian citizens, permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens to live in Australia indefinitely. This visa offers a pathway for parents to join their children and enjoy the benefits of permanent residency in Australia, including access to healthcare and the ability to work and study.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are parents of an adult Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen who meet the balance of family test and are willing to pay a higher visa application charge for faster processing compared to non-contributory parent visas.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143) is itself a permanent residency visa. After meeting residency requirements and other eligibility criteria, holders may apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.tax_implications: Visa holders are eligible for Australia's public healthcare scheme (Medicare). Eligibility for an Age Pension typically requires a 10-year qualifying residence period after the visa grant, and applicants must meet income, assets, age, and residence rules which are subject to change. The Assurance of Support is a bond intended to cover potential social security benefits accessed during the initial 10 years.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia permanently without restrictions.
Access Australia's public healthcare scheme (Medicare).
Eligible to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Sponsor other eligible family members for permanent residence.
Travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date the visa is granted.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., passport, birth certificates)
Evidence of relationship to sponsoring child
Sponsor documents (Form 40 Sponsorship for Migration)
Evidence meeting the Balance of Family Test
Character documents (police certificates from countries lived in for 12+ months since age 16)
Health examination results
Assurance of Support documents (when requested)
Proof of no outstanding debts to the Australian Government
application_process_steps: Prepare all required documents, including identity, relationship, and sponsor documents.
Sponsor lodges Form 40 (Sponsorship for Migration) and applicant submits Form 47PA (Application for a Contributory Parent visa) online via ImmiAccount.
Pay the first instalment of the visa application charge.
The application is placed in a queue for assessment; demand is high, leading to long processing times.
When requested, undergo health checks, provide police clearances, and provide an Assurance of Support.
Pay the second, larger instalment of the visa application charge when requested by the Department before a decision is made.

visas.name: Dependent Child visa (subclass 445)
visas.description: The Dependent Child visa (subclass 445) is a temporary visa for children of a temporary Partner visa holder, allowing them to stay in Australia while their parent's permanent Partner visa application is being processed. It ensures family unity during the migration journey.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for a biological, adopted, or stepchild who is dependent on a parent holding a temporary Partner visa (Subclass 309 or 820) or another Dependent Child visa (subclass 445), and whose parent has an ongoing permanent Partner visa application (Subclass 100 or 801).
visas.path_to_residency_description: Once the Dependent Child (subclass 445) visa is granted, the child must be added to their parent's permanent Partner visa application (Subclass 801 or 100) before a decision is made on the parent's application to continue their pathway to permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is temporary and cannot be extended. It is valid until a decision is made on the parent's permanent Partner visa application.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia temporarily.
Travel to and from Australia freely with multiple entry rights.
Access to Australia's healthcare system (Medicare) if eligible.
Enroll in free English language classes (Adult Migrant English Program) if eligible.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency by being included in the parent's permanent Partner visa application.
required_documents: Completed Subclass 445 Visa application form (Form 918).
Child's birth certificate or adoption papers (proof of relationship).
Proof of the sponsoring parent's temporary Partner Visa status (Subclass 309 or 820).
Parental consent documents (if one parent is not included in the application or if the child is under 18).
Medical examination results (for health requirements).
Police clearance certificates (for character requirements, if applicable).
Identification documents for the child (e.g., passport).
Evidence of financial dependency for children over 18 (e.g., bank statements, tax returns, money transfers, rent receipts).
Form 80 – Personal particulars for assessment, including character assessment (if child is above 16).
application_process_steps: Check if the child meets the eligibility criteria, including age, dependency, and the parent's visa status.
Gather all necessary supporting documents, such as birth certificates, passports, parental consent, financial dependency evidence, and health/character documents.
Complete the Subclass 445 Visa application form (Form 918).
Pay the required application fee.
Lodge the application, typically online via ImmiAccount or by sending it to the Child and Other Family Processing Centre.
Await a decision from the Department of Home Affairs and provide any additional information if requested.

visas.name: New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship (Temporary) visa (subclass 461)
visas.description: The New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship (Temporary) visa (subclass 461) is for non-New Zealand citizens who are members of the family unit of a New Zealand citizen living in Australia. This temporary visa allows eligible individuals to live, work, and study in Australia for up to five years. It facilitates family unity by enabling partners and dependent children of New Zealand citizens who hold a Special Category Visa (subclass 444) to reside in Australia.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-New Zealand citizen who is the partner or dependent child of a New Zealand citizen holding a Special Category Visa (subclass 444) in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Subclass 461 visa does not offer a direct pathway to Australian permanent residency or citizenship. Holders can explore other visa options, such as Partner Visas (e.g., Subclass 820/801 or 309/100) if eligible, skilled migration pathways (e.g., Subclass 189, 190), or employer-sponsored visas, depending on their individual circumstances, skills, and relationship status with an Australian citizen or permanent resident.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet eligibility criteria, provide updated evidence of the relationship with the New Zealand citizen, and the New Zealand citizen must maintain their Special Category Visa (subclass 444) status. Renewal may be possible even after a relationship breakdown if the applicant has spent at least two years in Australia in the last five years before applying, continues to meet health and character requirements, and has not formed a new family unit with another person (unless that person is also a 444 visa holder).
benefits: Live in Australia for up to 5 years.
Work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Travel freely in and out of Australia multiple times while the visa is valid.
Include eligible family members (partner/spouse, dependent children) in the application.
Renewable if eligibility criteria continue to be met.
required_documents: Proof of identity (e.g., passport, photo)
Relationship evidence (e.g., joint finances, household documents, correspondence proving genuine and continuing relationship)
Police certificates for each country lived in for 12+ months in the past 10 years
Health assessments or proof of private health insurance
Evidence of the New Zealand citizen's Special Category Visa (subclass 444) status
Birth certificates and other proofs of dependency for children (if applicable)
Completed Form 80 (Identity, Character and Employment Declaration)
application_process_steps: Check eligibility requirements for the visa, ensuring the New Zealand family member holds or will hold a Subclass 444 visa.
Gather all required documentation, including identity, relationship evidence, health, and character clearances.
Lodge the application online via an ImmiAccount.
Pay the applicable visa application fees.
Provide biometrics (if requested).
Await a decision on the application from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Orphan Relative visa (subclass 117)
visas.description: The Orphan Relative visa (subclass 117) is a permanent visa that allows a child who is single and without parents to care for them to come to Australia and live with an eligible relative. This visa provides a stable environment and familial support for children whose parents are deceased, permanently unable to care for them, or cannot be found.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a child under 18 years of age, who is single, has no parents able to care for them, and has an eligible Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen relative willing to sponsor them.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia upon approval. After residing in Australia and meeting eligibility requirements, the child may apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa grants permanent residency, so it is not 'renewable' in the traditional sense for staying in Australia. However, for travel outside Australia after the initial 5-year travel facility, the visa holder will need to apply for and be granted a Resident Return Visa (RRV) to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely as a permanent resident.
Work and study in Australia in line with Australian law.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date of visa grant.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible, after meeting residency requirements.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., passport showing photo, personal details, issue/expiry dates).
Four recent passport-sized photos (45mm x 35mm).
Evidence that the child has no parents capable of caring for them (e.g., death certificates, medical reports, official documents).
Evidence of the child's relationship to their relative (sponsor).
Written consent from everyone who can legally decide where the child lives, or evidence that the laws of the child's home country allow them to leave.
Character documents (if over 16 years of age).
Proof of payment of the application fee.
application_process_steps: Check eligibility criteria for both the child and the sponsoring relative.
Gather all required documents, including identity, parental care evidence, and relationship proof.
Ensure the child meets health and character standards.
Pay the visa application fee online and attach the payment receipt.
Submit the application by paper, as online lodgements are generally not accepted for this visa type.
The child must be outside Australia when the application is made and when a decision is made on the visa.

visas.name: Orphan Relative visa (subclass 837)
visas.description: The Orphan Relative visa (subclass 837) is a permanent visa for a single child already in Australia whose parents are deceased, permanently unable to care for them, or cannot be found. This visa allows the child to live permanently with an eligible Australian relative (sponsor) who is an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen.
visas.target_applicant: A single child who is generally under 18 years of age (with limited exceptions for those up to 25 with a disability or as a full-time student), is currently in Australia, has no parent capable of caring for them, and is sponsored by an eligible Australian relative.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency upon approval, allowing the child to live in Australia indefinitely. After satisfying specific residency criteria, the visa holder may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: This is a permanent visa and does not require renewal for stay. However, for travel in and out of Australia after the initial 5-year travel facility expires, a Resident Return (RRV) visa is required.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this permanent visa are subject to Australia's standard tax residency rules. No special tax treatment is specified for this visa category.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia.
Ability to live, study, and work in Australia indefinitely.
Access to Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Eligibility to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency criteria.
Ability to sponsor eligible family members for permanent residency.
Travel to and from Australia for up to five years from the date of visa grant (a Resident Return Visa is needed for re-entry after this period).
required_documents: Evidence of the child's orphan status (e.g., death certificates, medical reports showing permanent incapacity of parents, or official documents proving parents cannot be found).
Proof of the child's identity and age, such as a birth certificate.
Evidence of the child's relationship with the eligible Australian relative.
Character documents for the child if they are 16 years or older.
Health assessment results.
Consent for the child to migrate to Australia, if required.
Evidence that any outstanding debts owed by the child or their family to the Australian Government have been repaid or arrangements made for repayment.
Sponsorship application from the eligible Australian relative.
application_process_steps: Ensure the child meets the age and orphan status criteria, and other visa requirements.
Gather all necessary documents, including identity, relationship evidence, and health and character assessments.
The eligible relative completes the sponsorship application and it must be approved by the Department.
Complete the visa application form and provide all required information and documents.
Pay the relevant visa application fee.
Lodge the visa application (typically online or by mail, depending on current processes).
Arrange health examinations and provide police checks if requested.
Await the visa decision from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Parent visa (subclass 103)
visas.description: The Parent visa (subclass 103) is a permanent visa that allows parents of a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen to move to Australia permanently. It is part of the non-contributory parent visa stream, offering a lower application cost in exchange for significantly longer processing times.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a parent of an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen who is 'settled' in Australia, and who meets the 'Balance of Family Test'.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia from the outset. After residing in Australia as a permanent resident for a specified period and meeting other eligibility criteria, visa holders may apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: After the initial 5-year travel facility, holders must apply for a Resident Return Visa (RRV) to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident if they travel overseas.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely (permanent residency)
Work and study in Australia
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare
Sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia
If eligible, apply for Australian citizenship
required_documents: Valid passport
Documents proving you meet the Balance of Family Test
Completed Sponsorship for migration to Australia form (Form 40)
Proof of sponsor's relationship to you
Proof the sponsor is an eligible Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or New Zealand citizen
Assurance of Support documents (required after initial application)
Health examination results
Police clearance certificates (character requirements)
Signed Australian Values Statement
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet the eligibility criteria, including the Balance of Family Test and having an eligible sponsor
Gather all required documents, including identity, relationship, and character documents
Lodge the visa application online using ImmiAccount
Undergo health examinations and character checks
Provide Assurance of Support documents (requested after initial application)
Await decision (processing times are very long)

visas.name: Partner (Provisional and Migrant) visa (subclass 309/100)
visas.description: The Partner (Provisional and Migrant) visa (subclass 309/100) is a two-stage visa that allows the spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen to live in Australia permanently. The provisional Subclass 309 visa is granted first, followed by the permanent Subclass 100 visa, typically after a two-year assessment period.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who are outside Australia and are in a genuine and continuing spouse or de facto relationship with an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, seeking to live permanently in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Subclass 309 visa is the provisional stage, allowing temporary stay in Australia. Approximately two years after the initial application, the Department of Home Affairs reassesses the relationship to determine eligibility for the permanent Subclass 100 visa. In some cases, for long-term relationships, the permanent visa may be granted directly.
visas.renewal_conditions: To progress from the provisional (309) to the permanent (100) visa, the applicant must continue to be in a genuine and ongoing relationship with the same sponsor.
visas.tax_implications: Once granted the visa and residing in Australia, individuals are subject to Australia's standard tax residency rules. No special tax treatments are mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia.
Travel to and from Australia as many times as desired.
Enroll in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare (from the date of application for permanent residency, and while on the 309 visa).
Attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program if eligible.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency and eventually Australian citizenship.
required_documents: Evidence of a genuine and continuing relationship (e.g., financial commitments, nature of household, social aspects, mutual commitment, evidence of living together or not permanently apart).
Identity documents for both applicant and sponsor.
Marriage certificate (if married) or evidence of a de facto relationship.
Birth certificate of any dependent children included in the application.
Police clearance certificates from any country lived in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years for both applicant and sponsor.
Results of required medical examinations.
Completed sponsorship application (Form 40SP).
Evidence of Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or eligible New Zealand citizenship for the sponsor.
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility criteria are met by both the applicant and sponsor (applicant must be outside Australia, in a genuine relationship with an Australian citizen/PR/eligible NZ citizen, both 18+).
Gather all necessary documents and comprehensive evidence to demonstrate a genuine and continuing relationship.
Lodge the combined application for both Subclass 309 and 100 visas online and pay the application fee.
Undergo required health examinations and obtain police clearance certificates from all relevant countries.
Wait for the decision on the provisional Subclass 309 visa, which can be granted while inside or outside Australia (as of November 2023).
Approximately two years after the initial application, the permanent Subclass 100 visa will be assessed based on the ongoing genuine and continuing nature of the relationship.

visas.name: Partner visa (subclass 820/801)
visas.description: The Partner visa (subclass 820/801) is a two-stage visa that allows the spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen to live in Australia. The subclass 820 is a temporary visa, leading to the permanent subclass 801 visa after an assessment period, usually two years.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for individuals who are married to or in a genuine and continuing de facto relationship with an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, and wish to live together in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Partner visa (subclass 820/801) is a direct pathway to permanent residency. The subclass 820 is a temporary visa granted first, allowing the applicant to live in Australia while the permanent visa is processed. Approximately two years after the initial application, the relationship is reassessed, and if it remains genuine and ongoing, the subclass 801 (permanent) visa is granted.
visas.renewal_conditions: The 820 (temporary) visa is granted first, and its validity lasts until a decision is made on the permanent 801 visa. The 801 visa is permanent. To transition from the 820 to the 801, the relationship must continue to be genuine and ongoing, and all visa requirements must still be met.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Partner visa (subclass 820/801) are generally considered Australian residents for tax purposes, particularly if they intend to stay permanently and have ongoing ties like a job or home. They are typically eligible for the tax-free threshold and must declare all income, including foreign income (with some exceptions for temporary residents). They may also be required to pay the Medicare levy.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia indefinitely upon grant of the permanent 801 visa.
Travel to and from Australia as many times as you want.
Access Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia (after permanent visa grant).
Attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program if eligible.
required_documents: Valid passports and birth certificates for both applicant and sponsor.
Marriage certificate (if married) or evidence of a de facto relationship (e.g., proof of 12 months cohabitation or relationship registration).
Health examinations from approved panel doctors.
Police clearances from all countries lived in for 12+ months in the last 10 years.

Evidence of a genuine and continuing relationship across various aspects: financial, nature of household, social, and mutual commitment (e.g., joint bank statements, shared bills, lease agreements, photos, statutory declarations from friends and family, and personal statements).
Form 80 - Character Assessment (for applicant and accompanying dependent children aged 16 and over).
Form 888 - Statutory declarations from Australian citizens or permanent residents supporting the relationship (at least two recommended, often more).
application_process_steps: Prepare your application, gathering detailed evidence of your genuine and continuing relationship.
Lodge the combined 820/801 application online through ImmiAccount while you are in Australia.
Pay the visa application charge, which covers both the temporary and permanent stages.
Satisfy health and character requirements by undergoing medical exams and obtaining police checks.
The Department assesses the temporary 820 visa stage; if granted, you can live, work, and study in Australia.
Approximately two years after the initial application, provide updated evidence of your continuing relationship for the permanent 801 visa assessment.

visas.name: Prospective Marriage visa (subclass 300)
visas.description: The Prospective Marriage visa (subclass 300) is a temporary visa for individuals who want to come to Australia to marry their prospective spouse. It allows the visa holder to live, work, and study in Australia for 9 to 15 months, providing time to plan and organize their wedding before applying for a permanent Partner visa.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for individuals who are engaged to an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen and intend to marry them within 9 months of the visa grant.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After marrying your prospective spouse within the visa's validity period (9 to 15 months), you must apply for an onshore Partner visa (subclass 820/801) before your Prospective Marriage visa expires. The Partner visa leads to Australian permanent residency.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia for 9 to 15 months from the date the visa is granted.
Travel to and from Australia as many times as desired while the visa is valid.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency in Australia after marriage.
Allows inclusion of dependent family members in the application.
Eligible for a significantly reduced application fee for the subsequent Partner visa (subclass 820/801) after marriage.
required_documents: Personal identification documents (e.g., passport, birth certificate)
Police clearances from all countries lived in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years after turning 16
Health examination results
Evidence of genuine intention to marry (e.g., signed and dated letter from marriage celebrant, Notice of Intention to Marry - NOIM lodgement)
Evidence of having met the prospective spouse face-to-face as adults and knowing each other personally
Evidence of a genuine and continuing relationship (e.g., written statements showing relationship history, shared interests, future plans)
Sponsorship application by the Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen partner
Two Form 888s (statutory declarations from witnesses attesting to relationship genuineness)
Official translations for any documents not in English
application_process_steps: Ensure you are outside Australia when you apply and when the visa is granted.
Log in to ImmiAccount or create a new account.
Select 'New application', then 'Family', then 'Stage 1 – Partner or Prospective Marriage Visa'.
Complete the application form and attach all required supporting documents.
Pay the visa application charge.
Submit your application and provide your transaction reference number (TRN) to your sponsor so they can complete their sponsorship application.

visas.name: Remaining Relative visa (subclass 115)
visas.description: The Remaining Relative visa (subclass 115) is a permanent visa for individuals living outside Australia who wish to move to Australia to be with their only close family members. It is designed for applicants who have no other close relatives outside Australia, and whose only near relatives are Australian citizens, permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens usually living in Australia.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a person with no other close family members (parents, siblings, non-dependent children) outside Australia, and whose only remaining near relatives are settled Australian citizens, permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia immediately upon grant. After a qualifying period of permanent residency and meeting other criteria, visa holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: While the visa itself is permanent, the travel facility allows travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date of grant. To continue travelling after this period, a Resident Return Visa (subclass 155 or 157) must be applied for.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely as a permanent resident.
Work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible relatives to come to Australia for permanent residence.
If eligible, apply for Australian citizenship.
required_documents: Identity documents (passport or travel document, birth certificate, national ID).
Evidence of your relationship with the sponsor (e.g., birth certificates, family trees, statutory declarations).
Proof that you are the only remaining relative of an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen, including evidence to meet the Balance of Family Test.
Proof of the sponsor's Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or eligibility as a New Zealand citizen.
Police clearance certificates from every country you have lived in for 12 months or more over the last 10 years since turning 16, including your current country of residence.
Medical examination reports to meet health requirements.
Evidence of your current marital status (e.g., marriage certificate, single status certificate if applicable).
Two recent passport-sized photographs.
If applicable, evidence that dependent children are financially dependent on the main applicant (e.g., bank statements, money transfers, rent receipts).
Original Curriculum Vitae for each person 18 years or over included in the application.
Certified copy of death certificates or other official documentation for any deceased immediate family members (applicant's or spouse's).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, including identity proofs, relationship evidence, and character and health documents.
Ensure an eligible sponsor in Australia completes the sponsorship form (Form 40).
Complete the visa application form (Form 47OF) and attach all supporting evidence.
Lodge the paper application from outside Australia by mail or courier to the specified processing center.
Pay the visa application fee, which may be in two instalments.
Await the Department of Home Affairs' decision, noting that processing times can be very long due to capping and queuing.

visas.name: Remaining Relative visa (subclass 835)
visas.description: The Remaining Relative visa (subclass 835) is a permanent visa that allows individuals to stay in Australia to live with their only close family members. It is designed for applicants who have no other near relatives usually living outside Australia. [4, 8, 15]
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is someone whose all near relatives (parents, step-parents, siblings, step-siblings, non-dependent children) are Australian citizens, permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens, and who has no other near relatives living outside Australia or in Australia on a temporary visa. [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 15, 17]
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia, allowing indefinite stay. After meeting residency requirements, visa holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship. [4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 14]
visas.renewal_conditions: While the visa itself is permanent, the initial travel facility is valid for 5 years. To re-enter Australia as a permanent resident after this period, you will need to apply for and be granted a Resident Return Visa (RRV). [4, 6]
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely (permanent residency). [4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 14]
Work and study in Australia without restrictions. [4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14]
Enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare. [4, 6, 8, 9, 10]
Sponsor eligible relatives to come to Australia. [4, 6, 8, 10]
If eligible, apply for Australian citizenship. [4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 14]
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., valid passport, birth certificates). [5, 7, 12, 17]
Relationship proof (e.g., birth certificates, marriage certificates, adoption papers). [5, 7, 12, 17]
Evidence of no other close relatives usually living outside Australia. [5, 7, 12, 17]
Health assessments. [5, 7, 8, 12, 14, 17]
Police certificates from each country lived in for 12 months or more over the last 10 years after turning 16. [5, 7, 8, 14, 17]
Assurance of Support (when requested by the Department). [3, 7, 8, 14, 17]
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet eligibility criteria, including having an eligible sponsor and no other near relatives outside Australia. [7, 16]
Gather all required documents, such as identity, relationship, health, and character evidence. [5, 7, 12, 16]

Complete and submit the paper-based visa application form (Form 47OF and Form 40). From 23 July 2025, applicants can import their paper application into ImmiAccount to track its status online. [4, 7, 10, 16]
Pay the visa application charge in two instalments (first at application, second when requested by the Department). [3, 6, 7, 10]
Wait for the application to be processed. (Note: This visa is subject to capping and queuing, leading to very long processing times that can span many years). [4, 9, 11, 14, 16]
Attend any required interviews or provide additional information if requested by the Department of Home Affairs. [6]

visas.name: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870)
visas.description: The Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870) allows parents of Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens to visit Australia for an extended period, typically 3 or 5 years. This temporary visa facilitates longer family reunions without providing a pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a biological, legal (including adoptive), step-parent, or parent-in-law of an approved Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen sponsor, who wishes to stay in Australia temporarily for an extended period.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa does not directly lead to permanent residency or citizenship. It is a temporary visa only. Holders are generally not eligible to apply for other permanent parent visas while holding a Subclass 870 visa, unless they wait until it expires.
visas.renewal_conditions: Can be renewed for a maximum cumulative stay of 10 years. Applicant must generally be outside Australia for at least 90 days before lodging a further application. Sponsor and applicant must continue to meet eligibility requirements.
visas.tax_implications: Null. Standard resident tax rules apply if criteria are met. The visa is a contribution to the cost of services parents will use, as most visa holders will not have paid tax in Australia.
benefits: Extended stay in Australia for up to 3 or 5 years at a time, avoiding frequent departures and re-entries required by visitor visas.
No Balance of Family Test is required, unlike permanent parent visas, making eligibility more straightforward.
Opportunity to reunite with children and grandchildren in Australia for meaningful periods, addressing long waiting times for permanent parent visas.
Renewable for a total cumulative stay of up to 10 years.
Permits multiple entries to and from Australia during the visa validity period.
required_documents: Approved Parent Sponsorship (first step in the process).
Identity documents (e.g., valid passport, national identity card, proof of name change).
Proof of biological, legal, adoptive, step-parent or parent-in-law relationship with the sponsor.
Evidence of access to sufficient funds to support oneself in Australia.
Proof of adequate health insurance for the entire duration of stay in Australia.
Character documents (e.g., police certificates for countries lived in for 12+ months in the last 10 years).
Health examination results.
Evidence of genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily.
Sponsor's evidence of Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or eligible New Zealand citizenship.
Sponsor's evidence of at least four years of usual residence in Australia.
Sponsor's tax assessment notices or payslips confirming income.
application_process_steps: The Australian child applies to become an approved Parent Sponsor, meeting income, residency, and character requirements.
Once sponsorship is approved, the parent (applicant) receives permission to apply for the visa.
The parent lodges the visa application online within 6 months of sponsorship approval (or 60 days if permitted to apply in Australia).
The parent completes health examinations and provides biometrics if requested.
The Department of Home Affairs processes the application, potentially requesting additional documents.
A decision is made on the visa application.

visas.name: Business Innovation and Investment (Permanent) visa (subclass 888)
visas.description: The Business Innovation and Investment (Permanent) visa (subclass 888) is a permanent visa for holders of a provisional Business Innovation and Investment (subclass 188) visa, or in some cases a Special Category (subclass 444) or certain Business (Long Stay) (subclass 457) visa. It allows them to continue their entrepreneurial, investment, or business ownership activities and reside permanently in Australia. While the provisional BIIP program closed to new applications on July 31, 2024, the subclass 888 visa remains open for existing provisional visa holders.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who currently hold an eligible provisional Business Innovation and Investment (subclass 188) visa and have successfully operated a business or maintained an investment in Australia, demonstrating a commitment to continued economic contribution.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Business Innovation and Investment (Permanent) visa (subclass 888) grants permanent residency in Australia. Holders may apply for Australian citizenship after meeting standard residency requirements, typically four years of lawful residence in Australia, including at least one year as a permanent resident. Time spent on the provisional subclass 188 visa can count towards the four-year residency requirement.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa grants permanent residency. The associated travel facility is valid for five years; after this period, a Resident Return Visa (RRV) or another visa is required to re-enter Australia.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia permanently
Access Australia's public healthcare scheme (Medicare)
Apply for Australian citizenship after meeting eligibility requirements
Sponsor eligible relatives for permanent residence
Travel to and from Australia for five years from visa grant date
required_documents: Current or previous subclass 188 visa grant details
State/Territory nomination approval (or Austrade for Significant Investor/Premium Investor streams)
Evidence of business ownership and activity (e.g., ABN, business premises photos, profit & loss statements, balance sheets for the last 2 years, BAS statements)
Evidence of meeting stream-specific investment requirements (e.g., investment portfolio statements, compliance letters from fund managers)
Evidence of continuous physical presence in Australia as required by stream
Evidence of functional English or completion of an English course (or operating a High Performing Victorian Business for 888A in Victoria)
Police clearances for all applicants aged 16+
Health assessments if requested
Relationship documents for dependants (marriage/birth certificates)
Signed Australian Value Statement
Proof of no outstanding debts to the Australian government
application_process_steps: Confirm all obligations under the provisional Subclass 188 visa have been met for the relevant stream.
Obtain or renew a current nomination from an Australian state or territory government agency (or Austrade for specific streams).
Gather all required supporting documents demonstrating business performance, investment holdings, residency history, and health/character compliance.
Lodge the application online through the Department of Home Affairs' ImmiAccount.
Pay the visa application charge and upload all necessary evidence.
The Department of Home Affairs assesses the application against stream-specific criteria and may request additional information.

visas.name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) - Significant Investor Extension stream
visas.description: The Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) - Significant Investor Extension stream allows eligible holders of a subclass 188 visa in the Significant Investor stream to extend their stay in Australia for an additional two years, for a maximum total of two extension visas (four years). This visa facilitates the continuation of significant investment activity in Australia and provides a pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for individuals who currently hold a Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) in the Significant Investor stream for at least three years, or already hold a Significant Investor Extension stream visa (and have not held more than one extension visa), and continue to maintain their complying significant investment.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This provisional visa is a pathway to permanent residency through the Business Innovation and Investment (Permanent) visa (subclass 888) in the Significant Investor stream, provided the visa holder meets all eligibility criteria for the permanent visa, including residency requirements (e.g., living in Australia for at least 40 days per year for the duration of the provisional visa).
