visas.renewal_conditions: Hold a Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) in the Significant Investor stream for at least 3 years, or already hold a Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) in the Significant Investor Extension stream (and not have held more than one of these visas). Must be nominated by a State or Territory government agency or Austrade. Must continue to hold a complying significant investment continuously for the life of the provisional visa. Meet health and character requirements. Have functional English or pay the second instalment of the visa application charge. Uphold Australian values and have no debt to the Australian government.
benefits: Extend stay in Australia for up to 4 more years (two 2-year extensions).
Continue to carry out investment activity in Australia.
Includes eligible family members in the application.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency through the Business Innovation and Investment (Permanent) visa (subclass 888).
required_documents: Current nomination by a State or Territory government agency or Austrade.

Evidence of holding a Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) in the Significant Investor stream for at least 3 years, or an existing Significant Investor Extension stream visa (and not having held more than one previously).
Evidence of continuing to hold a complying significant investment, including recent holding statements for each investment (showing investor name, amount, and commencement date).
Form 1413D Declaration in relation to complying significant and premium investments (if applicable).
Evidence of functional English (or willingness to pay the second instalment of the visa application charge if required).
Documents supporting health and character requirements (medical examination results, police clearance certificates).
Signed Australian values statement.
Passport copy.
Evidence of no debt to the Australian government.
Evidence of not having had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused.
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility, including holding the relevant subclass 188 visa and maintaining your complying significant investment.
Obtain a current nomination from an Australian State or Territory government agency or Austrade.
Complete and submit the online application form through the Department of Home Affairs website.
Upload all required supporting documents and pay the visa application fee.
Undergo any required biometrics, health examinations, and police checks.
Await the visa decision from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: National Innovation visa (subclass 858)
visas.description: The National Innovation visa (subclass 858) is a permanent visa for individuals with an internationally recognised record of exceptional and outstanding achievement in eligible areas, such as a profession, sport, the arts, or academia and research. It replaced the Global Talent visa (subclass 858) on December 6, 2024. This visa aims to attract high-calibre individuals who can make a significant contribution to Australia's innovation, economy, and future industries.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an established or emerging leader with high-calibre talent and skills, demonstrating multiple internationally recognised achievements and the potential to genuinely shape Australia's future by contributing to key sectors of the economy.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants immediate permanent residency upon approval. After meeting specific residency requirements, visa holders are eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa grants immediate permanent residency. The initial travel facility allows travel to and from Australia for 5 years. After this, a Resident Return Visa (subclass 155 or 157) is required to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.
benefits: Immediate permanent residency for the visa holder and eligible family members.
Freedom to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia without employer sponsorship or state-specific conditions.
Access to Australia's public health care scheme (Medicare) and other government services and entitlements.
Opportunity to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Ability to sponsor eligible relatives for permanent residency.
required_documents: Invitation to apply for this visa (received after a successful Expression of Interest).
Proof of internationally recognised record of exceptional and outstanding achievement (e.g., awards, major publications, patents, leadership roles, endorsements).

Nomination for National Innovation Visa (Form 1000) from an eligible Australian citizen, permanent resident, eligible New Zealand citizen, or an Australian organisation with a national reputation in your field.
Valid passport.
Evidence of meeting health requirements (medical examinations and health clearances).
Evidence of meeting character requirements (police clearance certificates).
Evidence of functional English language proficiency or willingness to pay the second Visa Application Charge.
Curriculum Vitae or resume.
Other supporting documents as requested to prove eligibility and contributions to Australia.
application_process_steps: Assess genuine eligibility based on internationally recognised, exceptional and outstanding achievements in an eligible field.
Prepare and submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) to the Department of Home Affairs, showcasing achievements and potential contribution to Australia.
Await an invitation to apply from the Department of Home Affairs, typically within the validity of your EOI (usually 2 years).
Secure a nomination from an eligible Australian individual or organisation with a national reputation in your field.
Within 60 days of receiving an invitation, complete the online application form accurately, upload all required supporting documents, and pay the visa application fee.
Complete health examinations and provide police clearance certificates as required by the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186)
visas.description: The Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186) visa is a permanent residence visa for skilled workers who are nominated by an Australian employer. It allows them to live and work in Australia indefinitely and is designed to address skill shortages in the Australian labor market.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a skilled overseas worker with a genuine, full-time job offer from an approved Australian business.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The subclass 186 visa grants immediate permanent residency. After living in Australia for a specified period (generally four years, including at least one year as a permanent resident) and meeting other criteria, visa holders become eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself grants permanent residency and is not renewed. However, the travel facility, which is initially valid for 5 years, must be renewed by applying for a Resident Return visa to travel in and out of Australia after this period.
visas.tax_implications: Once granted permanent residency, visa holders are generally considered Australian residents for tax purposes and are subject to Australia's standard tax rules on their worldwide income. No special tax treatment is explicitly mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia from the date of visa grant.
Ability to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia indefinitely.
Access to Medicare, Australia's public health care scheme.
Can include eligible family members in the application.
A pathway to Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
required_documents: Nomination by an approved Australian employer for a genuine, full-time, permanent position.
Positive skills assessment (generally required for Direct Entry stream, with exemptions).
Competent English language proficiency (e.g., IELTS 6.0 in each band, or equivalent).
Identity documents (e.g., passport, birth certificate).
Health examination results.
Police clearance certificates from relevant countries.
Evidence of relevant work experience (at least 3 years for Direct Entry, 2-3 years for TRT stream).
Marriage certificate (if applicable, for partner inclusion).
Proof of relationship for dependent children.
application_process_steps: Step 1: The employer assesses eligibility and lodges a nomination application with the Department of Home Affairs, proving a genuine need for the role and adherence to salary and compliance requirements.
Step 2: The applicant ensures they meet all personal eligibility criteria, including age, English language, skills assessment (if applicable), health, and character requirements.
Step 3: The applicant gathers all required documents, including skills assessment, English test results, identity, and character documents.
Step 4: The applicant lodges the visa application online via ImmiAccount, either concurrently with or after the employer's nomination is approved, and pays the visa application charge.
Step 5: Await processing and respond to any requests for additional information or documents from the Department of Home Affairs.
Step 6: Receive a decision on the visa application.

visas.name: Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191)
visas.description: The Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191) allows eligible provisional visa holders who have lived, worked, and studied in designated regional areas of Australia to live and work in Australia permanently. It serves as the final stage of Australia's regional skilled migration pathway, transitioning temporary residents to full permanent residency with no regional restrictions after grant.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is ideal for individuals who have held a Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491) or a Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494) for at least three years, and have complied with their visa conditions, including regional residence and work.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Subclass 191 visa *is* a permanent residency visa. It offers a pathway to Australian citizenship after the visa holder has lived in Australia for a total of four years as a permanent resident (including time on the provisional visa), subject to meeting other citizenship requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself is permanent. However, the travel facility granted with the visa is for 5 years. To re-enter Australia as a permanent resident after this period, a Resident Return Visa (subclass 155) must be obtained.
visas.tax_implications: Once granted, holders of the Subclass 191 visa are Australian permanent residents and are subject to Australia's standard tax laws for residents. There are no special tax concessions or exemptions for this visa category.
benefits: Full permanent residency in Australia, allowing indefinite stay.
Unrestricted rights to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia (no regional restrictions after grant).
Access to Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
Ability to sponsor eligible family members for permanent residence.
Pathway to Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
required_documents: Valid passport and identity documents for all applicants.
Proof of holding an eligible provisional visa (Subclass 491 or 494) for at least 3 years.
Australian Taxation Office (ATO) Notices of Assessment for three income years within the eligible provisional visa period.
Evidence of living and working in a designated regional area for at least 3 years (e.g., payslips, employment contracts, utility bills, lease agreements).
Police clearance certificates from any country lived in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years since turning 16.
Health examination reports (if requested or previous ones have expired).
Marriage certificates, divorce documents, or death certificates (if applicable).
Signed Australian Values Statement.
Evidence of no outstanding debts to the Australian Government or arrangements to repay them.
application_process_steps: Ensure you have held an eligible provisional visa (Subclass 491 or 494) for at least three years.
Confirm you have lived and worked in a designated regional area of Australia for at least three years.
Gather Australian Taxation Office (ATO) Notices of Assessment for three income years during your eligible provisional visa period.
Obtain necessary health clearances and police certificates for all applicants.
Ensure compliance with all conditions of your previous provisional visa and sign the Australian Values Statement.
Lodge your application online through ImmiAccount, providing all required documents and paying the application fee.

visas.name: Pacific Engagement Visa (subclass 192)
visas.description: The Pacific Engagement Visa (subclass 192) is a permanent residence visa for citizens of participating Pacific island countries and Timor-Leste. It aims to deepen connections between Australia and the region by offering a pathway to permanent residency. Up to 3,000 visas, inclusive of partners and dependent children, are available annually through a ballot process.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a citizen of a participating Pacific island country or Timor-Leste, aged between 18 and 45 years, who is randomly selected in the ballot process and secures a formal, ongoing job offer in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Pacific Engagement Visa is a permanent residence visa, granting permanent residency upon approval. After a period of living in Australia and meeting eligibility criteria, visa holders may apply for Australian citizenship.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia
Ability to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia indefinitely
Access to Australia's universal healthcare system (Medicare)
Access to government-funded public schools and Commonwealth-supported university places
Eligibility to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements
Ability to sponsor eligible relatives to come to Australia
required_documents: Valid passport for a participating country
Evidence of birth in, or parent born in, an eligible country
Formal, ongoing job offer in Australia for the primary applicant or their partner
Evidence of English language proficiency
Health examination results
Police certificates (character documents)
Identity documents (e.g., birth certificate, proof of name change)
Relationship documents (for partners and dependent children)
Proof of adequate means to support self and family members
application_process_steps: Check eligibility criteria for the Pacific Engagement Visa ballot, including age and citizenship from a participating country.
Register for the PEV ballot online through the Department of Home Affairs' ImmiAccount during the open period, paying a non-refundable AU$25 registration fee.
Await random selection in the electronic ballot process.
If selected, receive a 'Notification of Selection' letter and must apply for the visa online within 120 days from the date of selection.
Secure a formal, ongoing job offer in Australia for the primary applicant or their spouse/partner.

Lodge the complete visa application online via ImmiAccount, including all required documents and paying the visa application charge of AU$335 for the primary applicant and AU$80 for each additional family member.
Undergo health examinations and provide police certificates to meet character requirements.
Await a decision on the visa application from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Regional Sponsored Migration Scheme (subclass 187)
visas.description: The Regional Sponsored Migration Scheme (subclass 187) visa is a permanent residency visa for skilled workers nominated by an employer in regional Australia. The Direct Entry stream is closed to new applications. Only the Temporary Residence Transition (TRT) stream remains open for specific transitional workers who previously held a Subclass 457 or Subclass 482 visa and meet certain work requirements in regional Australia.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for transitional subclass 457 or subclass 482 visa holders who have worked for their nominating employer in regional Australia for a specified period and are nominated for a permanent position.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency directly upon approval. Holders can apply for Australian citizenship if eligible.
benefits: Stay in Australia indefinitely (permanent residency).
Work and study in Australia.
Enroll in Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Valid passport and identity documents.
Evidence of holding a qualifying Subclass 457 or 482 visa during the transitional period.
Evidence of full-time employment with the nominating regional employer for the required period (2 or 3 years depending on transitional provisions).
English language test results (IELTS, PTE, OET, or equivalent) within the last 3 years.
Evidence of nominated occupation and any mandatory registration, licence, or professional membership.
Health examination results from a Department-approved panel physician.
Police certificates/character checks.
application_process_steps: Confirm transitional worker eligibility (held Subclass 457 on/after 18 April 2017, or Subclass 482 TSS in medium-term stream on/before 20 March 2019, and worked in regional Australia).
Employer confirms eligibility, operates in a designated regional area, and commits to offering full-time ongoing employment.
Employer engages a Regional Certifying Body (RCB) to confirm genuine need for the position and inability to fill locally.
Employer lodges the nomination application through ImmiAccount, paying the nomination fee and Skilling Australians Fund (SAF) levy.
Applicant lodges the visa application within six months of the nomination approval, providing personal details and evidence of skills.
Meet health and character requirements and provide English language test results.

visas.name: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494)
visas.description: The Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494) allows Australian regional employers to sponsor skilled overseas workers to fill genuine, full-time positions where a suitably skilled Australian worker cannot be found. This provisional visa enables skilled migrants to live, work, and study in designated regional areas of Australia for five years.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled workers under 45 years of age with at least three years of relevant work experience and competent English, who have been nominated by an approved regional Australian employer for an occupation on a relevant skilled occupation list.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the Subclass 494 visa for at least three years, living and working in a designated regional area, and complying with all visa conditions, holders may be eligible to apply for the Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191). While there is currently no minimum income threshold for the Subclass 191 itself, applicants must provide three years of ATO Notices of Assessment to demonstrate genuine economic participation.
visas.renewal_conditions: The Subclass 494 visa is a provisional visa valid for 5 years and is not directly renewable. It offers a pathway to permanent residency via the Subclass 191 (Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional)) visa after meeting specific eligibility criteria for at least 3 years, including living and working in a designated regional area.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Subclass 494 visa are generally considered Australian tax residents if they reside in Australia for 183 days or more, and are then taxed on their worldwide income. They are eligible for the tax-free threshold. Employers must pay the Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold (TSMIT) amount (AUD $79,499 from 1 July 2026) for the nominated position, along with superannuation contributions.
benefits: Live, work, and study only in designated regional areas of Australia for 5 years.
Travel to and from Australia as many times as you want while the visa is valid.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency (Subclass 191 visa) after 3 years, if eligible.
Allows inclusion of eligible family members, who can also live, work, or study in regional Australia.
Access to Medicare (Australia's public healthcare system).
required_documents: Current passport and identity documents.
Suitable skills assessment for the nominated occupation (unless an exemption applies).
Curriculum vitae (CV) or resume.
Qualifications and proof of work experience (e.g., employment references, payslips) demonstrating at least 3 years of full-time, relevant skilled work experience.
Proof of competent English language proficiency (e.g., IELTS 6.0 in each band or equivalent).
Health examination results.
Police clearance certificates (character documents).
Marriage certificate or proof of de facto relationship (if including partner).
Parental responsibility documents and consent for children under 18 (if applicable).
Documents for dependants over 18 (identity, character).
Evidence of employer nomination (approved by Regional Certifying Body (RCB) and Labour Market Testing results).
Employment contract or letter of offer.
application_process_steps: The employer applies to become an approved Standard Business Sponsor (if not already).
The employer obtains a positive assessment from a Regional Certifying Body (RCB) for the nominated position.
The employer undertakes Labour Market Testing to demonstrate no suitably skilled Australian worker is available.
The employer nominates an eligible occupation and the visa applicant.
The skilled worker prepares and lodges their visa application with all required documents, including a positive skills assessment and English language proficiency.
The applicant and any family members undergo health and character checks.

visas.name: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189)
visas.description: The Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189) is a permanent residency visa for invited skilled workers with in-demand skills and qualifications who are not sponsored by an employer, state, territory, or family member. It allows holders to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia indefinitely.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled professionals under 45 years old with an occupation on Australia's Medium and Long-term Strategic Skills List, who can meet a minimum points test threshold and do not require sponsorship.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189) is a permanent residency visa, granting permanent residency from day one. After holding this visa and meeting specific residency criteria (typically 4 years of residency including 12 months as a permanent resident), visa holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself is permanent. The multiple-entry travel facility, initially valid for 5 years, is renewable by applying for a Resident Return Visa (RRV) if you wish to travel to and from Australia after its expiry.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Australian resident tax rules apply, as no special tax treatment is mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Live, work, and study permanently anywhere in Australia.
Access to Medicare, Australia's public health care system.
Ability to sponsor eligible family members for permanent residence.
Pathway to Australian citizenship after meeting residency criteria.
Multiple-entry travel facility for 5 years (renewable).
required_documents: Positive skills assessment for nominated occupation
Evidence of competent English language proficiency (e.g., IELTS, PTE, TOEFL scores)
Proof of identity (e.g., passport)
Educational qualifications
Skilled employment history documentation
Partner and dependent family member documents (if applicable)
Police clearance certificates from all countries lived in for 12+ months in the last 10 years (post-16)
Health examination results
application_process_steps: Ensure your occupation is on the relevant Skilled Occupation List and obtain a positive skills assessment from the relevant authority.
Achieve at least a 'competent' level of English language proficiency.
Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect, meeting a minimum of 65 points on the points test (though higher scores are often needed to receive an invitation).
Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA) from the Department of Home Affairs during an invitation round.
Lodge your complete visa application online within 60 days of receiving the invitation, including all required documents and paying the application fee.
Undergo mandatory health examinations and provide police clearance certificates.

visas.name: Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)
visas.description: The Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) is a permanent residency visa for skilled workers nominated by an Australian state or territory government. It allows the holder to live and work anywhere in Australia permanently and contributes to filling local skills shortages in specific regions.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a skilled professional under 45 years of age with an occupation on a relevant state/territory skilled occupation list, who can meet a minimum points test threshold and is willing to live and work in the nominating state or territory for at least two years.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) is a permanent residency visa from the date of grant. After meeting residency requirements (generally living in Australia for four years, including one year as a permanent resident), holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is permanent, but the travel facility expires after 5 years. To re-enter Australia as a permanent resident after this period, a Resident Return (RRV) visa is required.
visas.tax_implications: Null, as standard resident tax rules apply upon becoming a permanent resident. No special tax treatment is mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Stay in Australia permanently and indefinitely.
Work and study anywhere in Australia.
Enrol in Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible relatives for permanent residence.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Current passport showing photo, personal details, issue and expiry dates.
Identity documents (e.g., birth certificate, national ID card).
Evidence of competent English language ability (e.g., IELTS, PTE, TOEFL, OET test results).
Suitable skills assessment for the nominated occupation.
Employment reference letters, payslips, bank statements, tax records, and superannuation details proving work experience.
Educational qualifications (degree certificates, academic transcripts, Confirmation of Enrollment if studied in Australia).
Police certificates from any country lived in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years since turning 16.
Relationship documents (e.g., marriage certificate, evidence of de facto relationship for 12 months).
Passport-sized photographs.
State nomination approval letter.
Curriculum vitae (CV) or résumé covering full employment and educational history over the past 10 years.
application_process_steps: Obtain a positive skills assessment for your nominated occupation from the relevant assessing authority.
Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect, indicating your nominated occupation, skills, and states/territories you are willing to live in.
Receive a nomination from an Australian state or territory government, which adds 5 points to your EOI score.
Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA) for the visa from the Department of Home Affairs (within 60 days of invitation).
Lodge your complete visa application online via ImmiAccount within 60 days of receiving the ITA, including all supporting documents and paying the visa fee.
Undergo required health examinations and provide police clearance certificates.

visas.name: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491)
visas.description: The Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491) is a 5-year provisional visa designed for skilled workers and their families who wish to live, work, and study in designated regional areas of Australia. It addresses skill shortages in regional Australia and provides a clear pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled migrants under 45 years of age who are nominated by an Australian state or territory government agency or sponsored by an eligible family member residing in a designated regional area of Australia, and who meet a minimum points test requirement.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the subclass 491 visa for at least three years, living, working, and studying in a designated regional area, and complying with all visa conditions, holders may be eligible to apply for the Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191). As of August 31, 2023, there is no minimum income threshold required for the 191 visa application; applicants need to show 3 years residency in a Designated Regional Area and provide income tax returns for 3 years.
visas.renewal_conditions: The subclass 491 visa cannot be extended. To stay in Australia after its expiry, holders must apply for a new visa, typically the Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191), if eligible.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Australian resident tax rules generally apply. Visa holders are required to submit income tax returns to demonstrate compliance with visa conditions, particularly for the pathway to permanent residency.
benefits: Live, work, and study in a designated regional area of Australia for up to 5 years.
Pathway to permanent residency (subclass 191 visa) after 3 years.
Access to Medicare (Australia's public healthcare system).
Can include spouse/de facto partner and dependent children in the application.
Travel to and from Australia multiple times while the visa is valid.
required_documents: Valid passport
Birth certificate
Skills assessment for nominated occupation
English language test results (Competent English minimum)
Expression of Interest (EOI)
State/Territory nomination or eligible family sponsorship documents
Health examination results
Police clearance certificates from countries lived in for 12+ months in the last 10 years
Documents proving claims made in EOI (e.g., educational qualifications, work experience, relationship documents for partners/dependants)
Tax assessment notices/payment summaries for income (for subsequent 191 PR application)
application_process_steps: Check occupation against relevant skilled occupation list.
Obtain a suitable skills assessment for the nominated occupation.
Sit an English language test and achieve at least 'Competent English'.
Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) through SkillSelect, achieving a minimum of 65 points.
Secure a nomination from an Australian state or territory government agency, or sponsorship from an eligible relative in a designated regional area.
Receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA) for the visa.
Lodge the visa application online via ImmiAccount with all required documents.
Complete health examinations and provide police clearance certificates.
Await visa grant decision.

visas.name: Skilled Regional visa (subclass 887)
visas.description: The Skilled Regional visa (subclass 887) is a permanent visa for skilled workers who have lived and worked in specified regional areas of Australia on a previous eligible visa. It allows holders to stay in Australia indefinitely, work and study anywhere in the country, and access public healthcare.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled workers who have successfully completed a period of living and working in regional Australia on a provisional skilled regional visa (such as subclasses 489, 495, 496, 475, or 487).
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa *is* permanent residency. After holding permanent residency for four years (including one year as a permanent resident immediately before applying) and meeting other criteria, holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself is permanent. The travel facility component of the visa is valid for 5 years from the date of grant. To continue travelling to and from Australia as a permanent resident after this period, a Resident Return Visa (subclass 155 or 157) must be obtained.
visas.tax_implications: As a permanent resident, standard Australian tax residency rules apply. There are no special tax concessions associated with this visa.
benefits: Stay in Australia permanently and indefinitely.
Work and study anywhere in Australia without restrictions.
Enrol in Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible relatives for permanent residence.
Apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., valid passport, national identity documents, birth certificate)

Work and residence documents (e.g., employment references on company letterhead, payslips, Notices of Assessment from Australian Taxation Office, bank statements, rental agreements, utility bills, title deeds)
Eligible provisional visa history documents (e.g., previous visa grant letters, travel history records)
Character documents (Australian police certificate and overseas police certificates if applicable)
Proof of functional English (unless exempted)
Relationship documents (if including family members)
Health examination reports (if requested)
Signed Australian Values Statement (for applicants over 18)
Evidence of compliance with conditions of previous eligible visa
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility by holding an eligible provisional visa (e.g., 489, 495, 496, 475, 487) and meeting residency and work requirements in a specified regional area.
Gather all necessary supporting documents, including identity, work, residence, character, and English proficiency evidence.
Lodge the visa application online via ImmiAccount, providing all required information.
Pay the visa application fee.
Complete any requested health examinations and provide police clearance certificates.
Await a decision from the Department of Home Affairs (must be in Australia when the visa is granted, unless COVID-19 concessions apply).

visas.name: Temporary Skill Shortage visa (subclass 482)
visas.description: The Temporary Skill Shortage visa (subclass 482), now operating under the Skills in Demand (SID) visa framework, is an employer-sponsored temporary work visa. It enables Australian employers to address labour shortages by bringing in skilled workers when suitably qualified Australian workers are unavailable. This visa allows skilled overseas professionals to live and work in Australia for their sponsoring employer.
visas.target_applicant: Skilled workers who have a job offer from an approved Australian employer and are nominated for a position on an eligible occupation list, meeting specific skill, English language, and income requirements.
visas.path_to_residency_description: All Subclass 482 visa holders, if eligible, can be sponsored by their employers for the Employer Nomination Scheme (ENS) Subclass 186 Temporary Residence Transition (TRT) visa. Eligibility typically requires working for the same employer for at least two years (reduced from three) in the nominated occupation. Periods of employment with any approved sponsor may count towards permanent residency requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew, applicants must maintain ongoing employer sponsorship and continue to meet the eligibility criteria for the visa, with employers paying the Skilling Australians Fund (SAF) levy upon renewal.
benefits: Work in Australia for an approved sponsor for up to 4 years (or 5 years for Hong Kong passport holders).
Study in Australia (without government assistance).
Travel to and from Australia multiple times while the visa is valid.
Potential pathway to permanent residence.
Include eligible family members in the visa application.
required_documents: Valid passport or other travel document
Skills assessment (if required for the nominated occupation)
Proof of English language proficiency
Employment references demonstrating at least 1 year of relevant work experience in the nominated occupation within the last 5 years
Health examination results
Police certificates and character checks
Evidence of job offer and employer nomination
application_process_steps: The employer must become an approved Standard Business Sponsor (SBS) or hold an approved Labour Agreement.
The employer nominates a position, outlining the job's tasks, duties, salary, and the skilled worker.
The candidate lodges the Skills in Demand (Subclass 482) visa application, providing all required supporting documents.
The application undergoes assessment, including health and character checks, before a decision is made.

visas.name: Global Special Humanitarian visa (subclass 202)
visas.description: The Global Special Humanitarian visa (subclass 202) is a permanent offshore humanitarian visa for individuals facing substantial discrimination or human rights abuses in their home country. It allows successful applicants to move to Australia permanently, work, and study, and eventually apply for citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for individuals who are outside Australia and their home country, are subject to substantial discrimination amounting to a gross violation of human rights, and have an eligible proposer in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is a permanent visa, granting permanent residency from the day of entry to Australia. Holders can apply for Australian citizenship after meeting standard residency requirements, typically four years of living in Australia with at least one year as a permanent resident.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply as this visa grants permanent residency.
benefits: Permanent residency status in Australia.
Freedom to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia indefinitely.
Access to government services and entitlements, including Medicare and education.
Opportunity to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Ability to propose certain family members for permanent residence.
required_documents: Evidence of persecution or significant discrimination in the home country.
Evidence of inability to seek protection from home country's authorities.
Form 842 – Application for an Offshore Humanitarian Visa (completed by the applicant).
Form 681 – Refugee and Special Humanitarian Proposal (completed by the proposer).
Identity documents.
Relationship documents (for proposer and family members).
Biometric data (if required).
Signed Australian Values Statement (if 18 years or older).
application_process_steps: Ensure the applicant is outside Australia and their home country, subject to substantial discrimination/human rights abuses, and has an eligible proposer.
The proposer submits Form 681 (Refugee and Special Humanitarian Proposal) online via ImmiAccount (mandatory from 1 July 2025).

The applicant receives a Transaction Reference Number (TRN) from the proposer and uses it to submit Form 842 (Application for an Offshore Humanitarian Visa) online via ImmiAccount within 60 days of the proposal (mandatory from 1 July 2025).
Gather and attach all required identity, humanitarian, and character documents, ensuring non-English documents are translated by accredited translators.
Attend any required interviews, provide additional information, and complete health and character checks.
Await visa decision from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Protection visa (subclass 866)
visas.description: The Protection visa (subclass 866) is a permanent visa for individuals who are currently in Australia and seek protection because they cannot safely return to their home country. It allows successful applicants to live, work, and study in Australia permanently. This visa is part of Australia's onshore humanitarian program for those who have arrived legally on a valid visa and engage Australia's protection obligations.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for people who are in Australia on a valid visa, meet Australia's protection obligations as a refugee or under complementary protection criteria, and have a well-founded fear of persecution or serious harm in their home country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Protection visa (subclass 866) is a permanent visa, granting permanent residency from the day it is granted. This status allows the visa holder to live indefinitely in Australia and provides a direct pathway to Australian citizenship once eligibility requirements (such as residency period and character checks) are met.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself is permanent, allowing indefinite stay in Australia. However, the travel facility component, which allows travel to and from Australia, is typically valid for 5 years and needs to be renewed to continue travelling.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia permanently.
Access government services such as Medicare (Australia's health care scheme) and Centrelink services.
Sponsor eligible family members for permanent residence through the offshore Humanitarian Program.
Opportunity to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date the visa is granted (travel facility requires renewal after 5 years).
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., valid passport, national identity card, birth certificate, proof of change of name).
Evidence supporting claims for protection, including detailed statements, police reports, testimonials, and medical reports.
Character documents, including police certificates for certain countries if requested.
Health examinations by Bupa Medical Visa Services.
Biometric data (fingerprints and photo).
Signed Australian Values Statement (for applicants over 18 years old).
Proof of relationship documents for including family members (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificates for dependent children).
History of any previous visas held in Australia.
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility by meeting criteria such as being in Australia on a valid visa and engaging Australia's protection obligations.
Gather all relevant and authentic documents, including identity, protection claims, health, and character documents.
Complete and lodge the application form (Form 866) online through ImmiAccount, paying the application charge.
Attend any required interviews and provide additional information or documents as requested by the Department of Home Affairs.
Undergo health examinations and provide biometric data (fingerprints and photo).
Await the visa decision, which will be communicated in writing. If refused, there may be options for appeal.

visas.name: Refugee visa (subclass 200)
visas.description: The Refugee visa (subclass 200) is a permanent visa for individuals who are outside Australia and are subject to persecution in their home country. It provides a pathway to protection and allows eligible individuals to live, work, and study indefinitely in Australia.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a person outside their home country, experiencing persecution, and typically referred by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) for resettlement in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Refugee visa (subclass 200) grants permanent residency upon entry to Australia. After meeting residency requirements, visa holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.tax_implications: Holders gain access to government services and entitlements, including Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare. Standard resident tax rules apply, but specific tax exemptions are not detailed for this visa category.
benefits: Permanent residency status in Australia.
Freedom to live, work, and study anywhere in Australia indefinitely.
Access to government services and entitlements, including Medicare, and free English language classes (510 hours).
Opportunity to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Ability to sponsor eligible family members for permanent residency.
required_documents: Evidence of refugee status, such as a referral from UNHCR or a protection visa application.
Fully completed and signed form 842 - Application for an Offshore Humanitarian visa.
Fully completed and signed form 80 (for applicants 18 and over).
Form 681 - Refugee and Special Humanitarian proposal (if you have a proposer in Australia), along with a certified copy of the proposer's Australian citizenship or permanent residence.
Passport pages showing photo, personal details, issue and expiry dates.
Six recent passport photos for each person included in the application.
Identity card and family book (true copies with authorized English translation).
Birth, marriage, divorce, and death certificates as relevant (true copies with authorized English translation).
Evidence of registration with any international organization dealing with refugees (e.g., UNHCR), if applicable.
Biometric data, if required.
Any additional documents relevant to claims of persecution.
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility criteria are met.
Gather all necessary documents.
Complete the visa application form (Form 842) and any other required forms (e.g., Form 681, Form 80).
Lodge the application, typically online via ImmiAccount (from 29 November 2025) or by mail to the Department of Home Affairs or appropriate overseas visa office.
Attend any required interviews or provide additional information as requested.
Await visa decision from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Emergency Rescue visa (subclass 203)
visas.description: The Emergency Rescue visa (subclass 203) is a permanent Australian humanitarian visa designed for individuals facing an immediate, real, and acute threat to their life or personal security in their home country. It offers a swift pathway to permanent residency in Australia, providing urgent protection and resettlement to those who cannot wait for standard humanitarian processing.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a person outside Australia who is subject to persecution in their home country and faces an immediate and urgent threat to their life or personal security, typically referred by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to the Australian Government for emergency resettlement.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is a permanent residence visa, allowing indefinite stay in Australia. Holders can apply for Australian citizenship after meeting specific residency requirements (typically living in Australia for four years).
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia, allowing indefinite stay.
Ability to work and study in Australia without restrictions.
Access to Medicare, Australia's public healthcare scheme.
Access to certain social security payments and the Humanitarian Settlement Program.
Pathway to Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Ability to propose immediate family members for permanent residence.
Travel to and from Australia permitted for the first five years.
required_documents: Form 842, detailing the immediate and severe threat to life or personal security.
Evidence of the compelling humanitarian emergency, potentially from relevant authorities or humanitarian organizations.
Valid identity documents.
Biometric data if required.
Health examination results (do not arrange until requested by the Department).
Police certificates (for character assessment).
Form 681 (Refugee and Special Humanitarian proposal) if a proposer is included (optional but can support the application and settlement).
application_process_steps: Ensure you are outside Australia and facing an immediate threat to life or personal security.
Be referred by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to the Australian Government for emergency resettlement (this is the primary pathway).
Complete and submit Form 842, providing a detailed account of the immediate and severe threat.
Meet health, character, and security requirements, including medical examinations and police checks.

Submit the visa application online through the Department of Home Affairs humanitarian visa application portal (paper-based lodgement is no longer accepted unless authorized for exceptional circumstances, as of July 1, 2025).
Await visa decision; urgent cases receive the highest processing priority within Australia's humanitarian program.

visas.name: Woman at Risk visa (subclass 204)
visas.description: The Woman at Risk visa (subclass 204) is a permanent Australian humanitarian visa designed for women and their dependent children who are living outside their home country and face victimisation, harassment, or serious abuse due to their gender. It offers a pathway to permanent residency and protection in Australia.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for women who are living outside both Australia and their home country, are without the protection of a male relative over 18, and are in genuine danger of gender-based victimisation, harassment, or serious abuse.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Subclass 204 visa is a permanent residency visa from the date of grant. Holders can apply for Australian citizenship after living in Australia for four years in total, with at least 12 months as a permanent resident, and meeting character and basic English requirements.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia from the date of grant.
Full work and study rights without restrictions.
Access to Medicare (Australia's health care scheme) and certain social security payments (Centrelink).
Eligibility to apply for Australian citizenship after meeting residency requirements (typically four years total, with at least one year as a permanent resident).
Free English language classes (510 hours AMEP) and settlement support grants.
required_documents: Personal identification documents (e.g., passport, birth certificate).
Statements detailing the risks and persecution experienced.
Evidence of gender-based violence, threats, harassment, or abuse.
Support letters from NGOs, community leaders, or UNHCR referral (if applicable).
Health assessments/medical examinations for all applicants.
Police clearance certificates/character references from countries lived in for over a year since turning 16.
Documents agreeing to respect Australian laws.
Proof of relationship for dependent family members.
Translations of non-English documents by accredited translators.
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility, which often involves a referral from UNHCR or a proposal from a close family member in Australia.
Gather all required documents, including evidence of persecution, identity documents, health assessments, and character certificates.
Complete and lodge the application form (Form 842 for offshore humanitarian visa), either online via ImmiAccount (from 29 November 2025) or by mail to an immigration office outside Australia.
Provide biometrics if requested.
Attend an interview if required.
Await decision from the Department of Home Affairs.

visas.name: Temporary Protection visa (subclass 785)
visas.description: The Temporary Protection visa (subclass 785) is a temporary visa for individuals already in Australia who arrived without a valid visa and seek asylum. It provides temporary protection and allows holders to live, work, and study in Australia, while engaging Australia's protection obligations but not meeting the criteria for a permanent Protection Visa (subclass 866).
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who arrived in Australia without a valid visa (e.g., unauthorized maritime arrivals, or those not immigration cleared) and are seeking asylum due to a well-founded fear of persecution or serious harm in their home country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: For eligible TPV holders who arrived in Australia before 14 February 2023, there is a pathway to permanent residency via the Resolution of Status Visa (Subclass 851). This permanent visa grants full permanent residency rights, including access to social security payments, the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), higher education assistance, the ability to sponsor family members, and eventually applying for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must apply for a subsequent Temporary Protection visa (TPV) before the current TPV expires and continue to engage Australia's protection obligations.
visas.tax_implications: TPV holders are generally considered 'temporary residents' for Australian tax purposes. They are typically taxed only on their Australian-sourced income and certain foreign employment income, but not on most foreign investment income. While eligible for Medicare, they are usually exempt from the Medicare levy but must apply for this exemption.
benefits: Live, work, and study in Australia temporarily for 3 years.
Access government services such as Centrelink, Medicare, and Workforce Australia.
Access short-term counselling for torture and trauma when required.
Attend free English language classes if eligible.
Eligible holders (who arrived before 14 February 2023) have a pathway to permanent residency via the Resolution of Status Visa (Subclass 851).
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., passport if available, national identity card, birth certificate, other documents establishing identity and nationality, with certified translations if not in English)
Evidence supporting protection claims (documents, statements, or other evidence of persecution or harm)
Health examination results from a Department-approved panel physician
Biometric data (fingerprints and photograph)
Police clearances (if available, or statutory declarations explaining why not)
Relationship documents (for included family members)
Signed Australian values statement
application_process_steps: Lodge a protection visa application online via ImmiAccount (or by post if unable to apply online), indicating wish for consideration for a Temporary Protection Visa.
Receive a Bridging Visa, allowing lawful stay in Australia while the application is processed.
Provide identity and biometric data for assessment and checks.
Attend any required interviews or provide additional information as requested by the Department.
Await visa decision from the Department of Home Affairs. If approved, the visa grants a 3-year stay.
If eligible, apply for a subsequent TPV before the current one expires, or apply for a permanent Resolution of Status Visa (Subclass 851).

visas.name: Safe Haven Enterprise visa (subclass 790)
visas.description: The Safe Haven Enterprise visa (subclass 790) is a temporary visa for people who arrived in Australia without a valid visa and are seeking asylum, allowing them to stay, work, and study for 5 years. It encourages economic and social participation in regional areas while providing temporary protection to eligible individuals.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an individual who arrived in Australia without authorisation, is in Australia, is unable to apply for a permanent Protection visa (subclass 866), and engages Australia's protection obligations.
visas.path_to_residency_description: For those who held or applied for a SHEV before 14 February 2023, there is a pathway to the permanent Resolution of Status (RoS) visa (Subclass 851). For others, meeting the 'SHEV pathway' requirements (42 months of full-time work or study in regional Australia) can unlock access to certain other permanent visas like skilled or family visas, but not a permanent Protection Visa (Subclass 866).
visas.renewal_conditions: Must still need Australia's protection and not be subject to any application bars.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Safe Haven Enterprise Visa are subject to Australian tax laws. Their tax residency status (Australian or foreign resident for tax purposes) will determine their tax obligations and is assessed by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) based on factors such as intention, purpose of presence, family/employment ties, and asset location, not solely on visa status.
benefits: Temporary residence in Australia for 5 years with full work and study rights.
Access to government services including Centrelink, Medicare, and short-term counselling for torture and trauma.
Pathway to permanent residency through the Resolution of Status visa (Subclass 851) for those who held a SHEV before 14 February 2023.
Opportunity to apply for other visas, including permanent skilled and family visas, by meeting the SHEV pathway requirements (42 months of regional work or study).
Family members can be included in the application.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., current or expired passports, birth certificate, national identity card, driver's licence, proof of name change).
Evidence of arrival in Australia.
Documents supporting claims for protection.
Character documents (e.g., police certificates for applicants over 16 who have lived in a country for 12 months or more in the past 10 years).
Relationship documents (if including family members).
Visa or residence permits (if applicable).
Biometric data (fingerprints and digital photograph) if required.
application_process_steps: Assess eligibility, confirming unauthorised arrival, ineligibility for Subclass 866, and engagement of protection obligations.
Gather all required identity, protection claim, character, and relationship documents.
Lodge the application online via ImmiAccount or by paper using Form 866.
Receive a Bridging Visa, allowing lawful stay while the SHEV application is processed.
Complete biometric data submission and health checks if requested.
Department of Home Affairs assesses the application and makes a decision.

visas.name: Resolution of Status visa (subclass 851)
visas.description: The Resolution of Status (RoS) visa (subclass 851) is a permanent visa designed for individuals who held or applied for a Temporary Protection visa (TPV) or Safe Haven Enterprise visa (SHEV) and arrived in Australia before 14 February 2023. It grants permanent residency, allowing holders to live, work, and study in Australia indefinitely.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a current or former holder (whose visa was not cancelled) of a Temporary Protection visa (subclass 785) or a Safe Haven Enterprise visa (subclass 790) who first arrived in Australia before 14 February 2023, and meets identity, security, health, and character requirements.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Resolution of Status visa (subclass 851) *is* a permanent residency visa. Holders may apply for Australian citizenship after meeting the standard residency requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself is permanent. However, the travel facility linked to the visa expires after 5 years, requiring an application for a Resident Return Visa (RRV) to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.
benefits: Permanent residency in Australia.
Ability to live, work, and study in Australia indefinitely.
Access to government services, including Medicare and Centrelink.
Opportunity to sponsor eligible family members for permanent residence.
Pathway to Australian citizenship.
required_documents: Identity documents (e.g., passports, birth certificates, biometrics like fingerprints and digital photograph).

Character documentation, including an Australian Federal Police (AFP) clearance certificate and potentially clearances from other countries where the applicant lived for 12 months or more since age 16.
Health examination results (may be waived if already satisfied for TPV or SHEV).
Evidence of current or previous Temporary Protection Visa (TPV) or Safe Haven Enterprise Visa (SHEV) (e.g., visa grant letters, ImmiAccount records).
Australian values statement (if 18 years or older).
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility, including holding or having applied for a TPV or SHEV before 14 February 2023, and being in Australia at the time of application.
For current TPV or SHEV holders without a pending application, apply online via ImmiAccount before the current visa expires.
If a TPV or SHEV application was pending before 14 February 2023, the application will be automatically converted to a RoS visa application; no separate application is needed.
Provide required documentation, including identity, health, and character information.
Attend any required interviews or provide additional information as requested by the Department of Home Affairs.
Await visa decision, with most applications expected to be processed within 12 months of processing commencement.

visas.name: Former Resident visa (subclass 151)
visas.description: The Former Resident visa (subclass 151) is a permanent visa that allows eligible individuals who were former Australian permanent residents or certain people who served in the Australian Defence Force to live in Australia permanently. It facilitates their return to Australia as permanent residents.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is ideal for former Australian permanent residents who meet specific 'long residence' criteria or individuals who served in the Australian Defence Force and wish to re-establish permanent residency in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa grants permanent residency in Australia from the date of grant. After meeting residency requirements, holders may be eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa itself is permanent, so it does not need renewal. However, the travel facility for leaving and re-entering Australia is valid for 5 years. After this period, a Resident Return Visa (RRV) must be obtained to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.
benefits: Stay in Australia permanently, with indefinite residency rights.
Work and study anywhere in Australia.
Enrol in Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
Sponsor eligible relatives to come to Australia.
Opportunity to apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
required_documents: Identity documents (current passport, national ID, proof of name change if applicable).
Documents proving long residence in Australia and maintained ties to Australia (e.g., social dependency, frequent visits, property ownership, business interests).
Evidence of service with the Australian Defence Force before 1981 (if applicable).
Character documents (police certificates from countries lived in for 12 months or more over the past 10 years after turning 16). Do not arrange until requested.
Health documents. Do not arrange health examinations until requested.
Partner documents (if applicable).
Child/dependent family member documents (birth certificate, adoption papers, consent forms for children under 18).
Form 47SV (Application for Special Migration to Australia).
Form 47a (Details of child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over), if applicable.
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility criteria are met for either the long residence or defence service stream.
Gather all required supporting documents.
Complete Form 47SV 'Application for Special Migration to Australia' and any other relevant forms (e.g., Form 47a for dependants).
Pay the visa application charge, typically online via ImmiAccount before lodging the paper application.
Mail the completed paper application form and supporting documents to the Department of Home Affairs' Perth office in Western Australia or Sydney office.
Await visa decision. Applicants must be in Australia if applying from within Australia, or outside Australia if applying from outside Australia, when the visa is granted.

visas.name: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602)
visas.description: The Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602) is a temporary visa for individuals seeking medical treatment, consultations, or organ donation in Australia. It also allows individuals to support a patient or organ donor holding this visa. The visa permits a stay for the duration of the treatment or consultation plan.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants include patients requiring medical care in Australia, organ donors, and individuals providing essential support to a patient or organ donor.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is a temporary visa and does not provide a pathway to permanent residency or citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must apply for a further Medical Treatment (subclass 602) visa from within Australia before the current visa expires, supported by updated medical evidence from your treating Australian specialist.
benefits: Receive medical treatment or consultation in Australia.
Donate an organ to someone in Australia.
Support someone who holds this visa (patient or organ donor).
Be granted single or multiple entries to Australia.
Study for up to 3 months, with longer periods possible if exemption criteria are met.
required_documents: Valid passport or other travel document.
Letter from your treating doctor in Australia outlining medical condition, required treatment, estimated timeframe, and cost.
Proof of financial capacity to cover travel, medical treatment, other expenses in Australia, and expenses of any accompanying person.
Evidence that payment of costs will not be a charge on the Australian government, or approval from the relevant government authority.
Identity documents (e.g., birth certificate, passport pages with photo and details).
Health insurance covering the duration of your stay (recommended).
Character documents.
Documents for applicants under 18 years old (if applicable).
One passport-size photograph (not more than six months old).
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet eligibility criteria, including health and character requirements.
Gather all necessary documents, including medical evidence and financial proof.
Complete the online application via the Department of Home Affairs website.
Undergo required health examinations and character assessments.
Receive visa decision and, if approved, commence medical treatment in Australia.

visas.name: Special Category visa (subclass 444) (for New Zealand citizens)
visas.description: The Special Category visa (subclass 444) is a temporary visa granted automatically to most New Zealand citizens upon their arrival in Australia, provided they hold a valid New Zealand passport and meet certain health and character requirements. It allows them to visit, study, stay, and work in Australia indefinitely. The visa ceases when the holder leaves Australia, but a new one is generally granted upon re-entry.
visas.target_applicant: New Zealand citizens holding a valid New Zealand passport who wish to visit, live, work, or study in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: From 1 July 2023, eligible New Zealand citizens holding an SCV (subclass 444) can apply directly for Australian citizenship without needing to first obtain permanent residency, provided they have resided in Australia for four years. All Subclass 444 visa holders are now considered permanent residents for citizenship purposes. Previously, some New Zealand citizens could apply for permanent residency through pathways like the Skilled Independent Visa (subclass 189) New Zealand Stream, which closed to make way for the direct citizenship pathway.
visas.renewal_conditions: A new Special Category visa (subclass 444) is granted each time an eligible New Zealand citizen enters Australia, provided they continue to meet eligibility requirements.
visas.tax_implications: New Zealand citizens on a Subclass 444 visa are generally classed as 'temporary residents' for tax purposes, meaning they typically pay tax only on Australian-sourced income. Most foreign-sourced income or capital gains are not taxable in Australia under this status. However, this temporary resident tax status can be lost if the individual is in a spousal or de-facto relationship with an Australian resident or citizen, leading to potential taxation on worldwide income.
benefits: Ability to live, work, and study in Australia indefinitely.
Automatic visa grant upon arrival in Australia for eligible passport holders.
Access to Medicare for eligible SCV holders.
Direct pathway to Australian citizenship for eligible New Zealand citizens from 1 July 2023.
Can travel freely in and out of Australia (visa ceases upon departure, new one granted on re-entry).
required_documents: Valid New Zealand passport.
Completed Incoming Passenger Card (for on-arrival processing).
application_process_steps: Ensure you hold a valid New Zealand passport.
Meet health and character requirements (not a behaviour or health concern non-citizen).
Present your valid New Zealand passport and a completed Incoming Passenger Card to an Australian Border Force officer upon arrival in Australia.
The Special Category visa (subclass 444) is automatically granted upon entry if eligibility is met.

visas.name: Investor Retirement visa (subclass 405) (for existing holders only)
visas.description: The Investor Retirement visa (subclass 405) is a temporary visa for self-funded retirees aged 55 or older who wish to live in Australia during their retirement years. This visa is closed to new applicants, but existing holders can apply for renewal to extend their stay.
visas.target_applicant: Existing Investor Retirement visa (subclass 405) holders or former holders who have not held another substantive visa since last entering Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A pathway to permanent residence for retirement visa holders commenced on 17 November 2018 for those who were granted their 405 visa before 8 May 2018. Further details on eligibility and requirements can be found on the Department of Home Affairs website under 'Pathway to permanent residence for Retirees'.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must fulfil all visa requirements from the previous period, maintain the designated investment, meet ongoing income and asset thresholds, and receive state sponsorship approval again. The designated investment amount may decrease upon the first renewal.
visas.tax_implications: Null. Standard Australian tax residency rules apply, and there are no special tax treatments mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Temporary residency in Australia for four years, with options for renewal.
Ability to work in Australia for up to 40 hours per fortnight.
Partner can be included on the visa.
Freedom to travel in and out of Australia multiple times during the visa validity period.
Enjoyment of Australia's lifestyle, culture, and natural beauty.
required_documents: Evidence of maintained designated investment (e.g., in state treasury corporation bonds)
Evidence of sufficient annual income
Evidence of assets (if applicable, for initial or state-specific requirements)
Evidence of health insurance coverage for the duration of stay
Health examination results
Character clearance (police certificates)
State/Territory sponsorship approval
Temporary Retirees Visa application form
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet the ongoing eligibility criteria for renewal.
Contact the relevant state or territory migration agency (e.g., Migration Queensland, NSW Government) to request renewal documents and re-apply for sponsorship.
Maintain or adjust your designated investment in the sponsoring state or territory's treasury corporation as per renewal requirements.
Complete and lodge the Temporary Retirees Visa application form.
Complete and lodge the State/Territory sponsorship form.
Pay the relevant application fee(s).

visas.name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188) - Business Innovation stream (closed to new applications as of 31 July 2024)
visas.description: This provisional visa was for individuals with proven business skills who sought to establish, develop, and manage a new or existing business in Australia. It offered a pathway to permanent residency and allowed visa holders to live, work, and study in Australia. Please note, this stream closed to new applications on 31 July 2024.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant was a successful business owner or manager under 55 years old, with a history of significant business turnover and net assets, nominated by an Australian state or territory government, and committed to owning and operating a business in Australia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This provisional visa provides a pathway to permanent residency through the Business Innovation and Investment (Permanent) visa (subclass 888) in the Business Innovation stream. After fulfilling certain requirements (e.g., operating a qualifying business in Australia for a specified period and meeting investment criteria) while holding the subclass 188 visa, applicants could apply for the permanent subclass 888 visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: Holders of the subclass 188 Business Innovation stream visa could apply for a Business Innovation Extension stream visa for an additional 2 years (total maximum of 6 years provisional visa validity). Conditions included holding the 188 visa for at least 3 years, demonstrating a need to be resident in Australia to operate the main business, and maintaining ownership and active operation in the nominated state/territory.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Australian resident tax rules apply to visa holders once they establish tax residency in Australia. No special tax treatment for this visa category was specified.
